newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Yankee owners say likely to shut nuke plant.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Yankee owners say likely to shut nuke plant.

text.p: Owners of the 582 megawatt Connecticut Yankee nuclear power plant in Haddam Neck, Conn., said Wednesday that an economic analysis of plant operations and costs of replacement power made a decision to permanently shut the plant likely.
"This was an economic study that began about a month ago and the analysis does not bode well for the plant to continue to operate," plant spokesman Anthony Nericcio told Reuters.

Under many of the scenarios evaluated, there was an economic disadvantage to continue running the plant, with costs ranging from tens of millions of dollars to as high as $100 million, the company said in a statement.
But Nericcio said the actual decision to mothball the plant has not been made yet.
"It will have to be made by a vote of all the owners, and it will probably take a month or more for the vote to take place," he said.

Connecticut Yankee is owned by eight utilities, with Northeast Utilities the principal owner and operator with 49 percent. Other owners include New England Power Co with 15 percent; United Illuminating Co with 9.5 percent; Boston Edison Co with 9.5 percent; Central Maine Power Co with six percent; Montaup Electric Co with 4.5 percent; Cambridge Electric Light Co with 4.5 percent; and Central Vermont Public Service Corp with two percent.

In the event of a permanent shutdown, each owner will make arrangements to purchase replacement power to make up for the lost generating capacity at Connecticut Yankee, something they have been doing since a refueling outage began in July.
Connecticut Yankee began the outage on July 22, but as a result of the analysis, work on the plant has been slowed pending a final decision.

"At this point, the economic picture does not seem favorable. But if a decision is made to close the plant, we are committed to doing so in a safe and orderly manner and to meeting all of Connecticut Yankee's obligations," president Bruce Kenyon said in the statement.
Connecticut Yankee is one of the oldest commercial nuclear power plants in th nation. Its operating license from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission expires in 2007.
